attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: The missing Yang-Mills estimate is a controlled computation or bound of the reflected Wilson boundary OPE for triples and quadruples: enough to prove zero quotient holonomy plus PSD modulus quotient, or to exhibit a determinant falsifier. Current RG compactness does not yet control the boundary anomaly B with phase and modulus resolution.
steps: Start with fixed collar observables W_i^\delta supported in t>\delta. Regulated reflection positivity and RG convergence give N^\delta\to N with N\ge0; this step is valid by the closed cone in the topology of finite reflected OS forms.

Use the boundary trace ansatz N_{ij}=B_{ij}M_{ij}+A_{ij}. Diagonal trace continuity gives A_{ii}=0; if A is a positive contact matrix, Cauchy-Schwarz implies A=0, so the remaining bridge is M=B^{[-1]}\circ N.

Normalize diagonals and set q_{ij}=N_{ij}/B_{ij}. Diagonal unitary congruence can change edge phases but cannot change cycle holonomy H_C=\arg\prod_{(ij)\in C}q_{ij}; therefore nonzero holonomy is an immediate phase falsifier for same-theory OS positivity.

If all quotient holonomies vanish, choose phases u_i so u_i^*M_{ij}u_j is real nonnegative. The remaining question is whether the modulus quotient matrix |N_{ij}|/|B_{ij}| is PSD on every realized finite Wilson family.

Local boundary OPE then predicts |B_{ij}| through a connected footprint kernel. If its log cross-ratios vanish, the modulus factor is just diagonal congruence and the bridge promotes; if not, one must test actual finite determinants of B^{[-1]}\circ N.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: The closed-cone part proves positivity of N, not of M. Without a same-theory theorem identifying B as diagonal-congruence trivial, or a direct proof that B^{[-1]}\circ N is PSD for all realized Wilson families, the argument could be proving OS positivity for a boundary-renormalized theory instead of the intended continuum Yang-Mills Schwinger functions.

assumptions: The collar limit topology controls every finite reflected Wilson matrix entry N_{ij}.
Diagonal trace continuity holds, so positive additive boundary contacts vanish by zero diagonal plus Cauchy-Schwarz.
B_{ij} is nonzero on the tested finite support graph and is the full multiplicative boundary anomaly for mixed reflected Wilson products.
The locked Wilson observables are the same before and after collar removal; no boundary-local observable is silently added.
definitions: source object: fixed-collar reflected Wilson OS matrices N^{\delta}_{ij}=S(\Theta W_i^\delta,W_j^\delta) with N=\lim_{\delta\downarrow0}N^\delta\ge0 by the valid closed-cone passage.

target object: intended continuum Wilson OS matrix M_{ij}=S(\Theta W_i,W_j) in the locked gauge-invariant test algebra, before adding boundary counterterms or renormalized reflection-plane observables.
controlled interface: multiplicative boundary anomaly B_{ij}\ne0 satisfying N_{ij}=B_{ij}M_{ij}+o(1) for every finite reflected Wilson pairing; hence M=B^{[-1]}\circ N if additive contacts vanish.

same-theory condition: B may be absorbed only by a diagonal nonzero congruence already fixed in the observable normalization; any non-coboundary phase or non-PSD realized quotient is a falsifier for this bridge, even if a modified boundary theory remains positive.
normalized quotient q_{ij}=N_{ij}/B_{ij} with q_{ii}=1 after diagonal normalization.
triangle quotient holonomy H_{ijk}=\arg(q_{ij}q_{jk}\overline{q_{ik}}), invariant under diagonal unitary changes of Wilson representatives.

equations.label: multiplicative trace quotient
equations.valid_when: Valid only after additive contacts are ruled out and B is computed in the same Wilson normalization used to define the target continuum Schwinger functions.

equations.label: phase coboundary criterion
equations.latex: \exists u_i\in U(1):\ \arg q_{ij}=\arg u_i-\arg u_j\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad H_{ijk}=0\ \text{for every triangle }(i,j,k)
equations.valid_when: Valid on each connected finite support graph with nonzero q_{ij}; for sparse graphs the condition is imposed on every cycle, not only literal geometric triangles.

equations.label: post-phase modulus determinant
equations.latex: \det M_{I}\ge0\quad\text{for all finite }I,\qquad M_{ij}=|N_{ij}|/|B_{ij}|\ \text{after phase removal}
equations.valid_when: Valid as the remaining OS test exactly when quotient phases have been gauged away by diagonal unitary congruence.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: Find three locked Wilson hairpins with H_{123}\ne0, or with H=0 but det(|N_{ij}|/|B_{ij}|)<0 after diagonal normalization.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Splits the Wilson boundary obstruction into a gaugeable phase part and a real modulus PSD part, giving a finite matrix bridge from collar positivity to target OS positivity.
candidate_lemmas.statement: For a finite locked Wilson collar family, same-theory OS positivity across the reflection plane is equivalent to positivity of the Hadamard quotient matrix after removing only a diagonal phase coboundary. The phase obstruction is the triangle holonomy; the remaining modulus obstruction is an ordinary real Gram-quotient determinant problem on the realized Wilson cone, not on all positive matrices.

assumptions: Boundary OPE coefficients for collar-colliding Wilson pairs have a local expansion depending only on coincident footprints and tangential data.
The dense Wilson core is closed under small collar deformations and finite linear combinations.
No reflection-plane cusp renormalization survives in single Wilson diagonals after the chosen same-theory normalization.
definitions: boundary footprint \partial C is the set where the collar family approaches the reflection plane.
log-modulus anomaly L_{ij}=\log |B_{ij}|, with diagonal entries absorbed into individual Wilson normalizations.
modulus cross-ratio K_{ij;k\ell}=L_{ij}+L_{k\ell}-L_{i\ell}-L_{kj}, which vanishes for rank-one boundary factors.

equations.label: rank-one modulus test
equations.valid_when: Valid for strictly positive |B_{ij}| on the finite tested family; zeros require restricting to connected nonzero blocks.

equations.label: connected kernel obstruction
equations.valid_when: Valid when L_{ij} is the full connected part of the boundary OPE and all one-body terms have been assigned to r_i.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: A nonzero connected footprint kernel producing K_{ij;k\ell}\ne0 is a falsifier unless realized collar correlations N are too small to detect it.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Turns the real modulus half of the bridge into a local boundary-OPE calculation instead of an abstract Schur multiplier question.
candidate_lemmas.statement: If the reflected Wilson boundary OPE is local along coincident reflection-plane footprints, then the first modulus obstruction should be expressible as a connected boundary covariance kernel; vanishing of its cycle sums promotes the modulus quotient to a diagonal congruence on a dense core.

control_decision.pivot_test: Pivot if RG estimates cannot resolve B beyond diagonal entries, or if Wilson boundary OPE necessarily introduces non-coboundary phase/modulus defects in the locked algebra.
control_decision.promotion_test: Promote if one proves zero quotient holonomy and PSD modulus quotient for a dense mirror-smooth Wilson core, with collar convergence valid for all finite reflected OS forms.
control_decision.reason: The branch is still producing sharper proof obligations: the target has moved from generic reflection-positivity closure to a computable boundary-OPE invariant for finite Wilson families.

dependency_updates.description: The valid closed-cone passage now feeds a finite Schur-preimage test: collar positivity gives N>=0, while same-theory OS positivity requires B^{[-1]} circ N>=0 after boundary anomaly analysis.
dependency_updates.status: formal part stable; Wilson boundary OPE gap open

dependency_updates.description: The algebra must be locked before collar removal, because absorbing non-coboundary B by adding boundary observables changes the theory.
Topology must converge reflected Wilson entries with enough resolution to identify B, quotient holonomy, and modulus determinants, not merely scalar Schwinger limits.

falsifiers: A three-hairpin Wilson family with nonzero quotient cycle holonomy H_{123}; this is a phase falsifier even if every two-by-two minor is valid.
A phase-trivial triple with det(|N_{ij}|/|B_{ij}|)<0 after diagonal normalization.
A nonzero connected boundary OPE kernel C_\partial for coincident reflection-plane footprints that creates K_{ij;k\ell}\ne0 and is detected by realized collar correlations.
A proof of reflection positivity only for an enlarged algebra containing boundary Wilson counterterms, not for the locked same-theory gauge-invariant algebra.
branch_outputs.mathematical_learning: Cycle 203 learned that the post-collar obstruction has a clean two-stage finite-matrix form: first remove quotient phases exactly when cycle holonomy vanishes; then test the real modulus quotient for PSD on realized Wilson families. This avoids the earlier overclaim that B alone decides failure. A nonzero boundary Gram anomaly is a falsifier only when its phase holonomy or modulus minors are detected by the locked Wilson OS matrices; otherwise it may be invisible to the realized cone.
branch_outputs.next_experiment: Compute the reflected boundary OPE for the simplest three Wilson hairpins with one shared reflection-plane footprint: extract B_{ij}, form q_{ij}=N_{ij}/B_{ij}, test H_{123}, then test det(|N_{ij}|/|B_{ij}|).
